name: grep
description: Matches patterns in input text. Supports simple patterns and regular expressions

options.name: --help
options.description: Print a usage message briefly summarizing these command-line options and the bug-reporting address, then exit

name: -E
--extended-regexp
options.description: Interpret PATTERN as an extended regular expression (-E is specified by POSIX.)

name: -F
--fixed-string
options.description: Interpret PATTERN as a list of fixed strings, separated by newlines, any of which is to be matched. (-F is specified by POSIX.)

name: -G
--basic-regexp
options.description: Interpret PATTERN as a basic regular expression (BRE, see below). This is the default

name: -e
--regexp
options.description: Use PATTERN as the pattern. This can be used to specify multiple search patterns, or to protect a pattern beginning with a hyphen (-).

name: -i
--ignore-case
-y
options.description: Ignore case distinctions in both the PATTERN and the input files. (-i is specified by POSIX.)

name: -v
--invert-match
options.description: Invert the sense of matching, to select non-matching lines. (-v is specified by POSIX.)

name: -w
--word-regexp
options.description: Select only those lines containing matches that form whole words.

name: -x
--line-regexp
options.description: Select only those matches that exactly match the whole line. (-x is specified by POSIX.)

name: -c
--count
options.description: Suppress normal output; instead print a count of matching lines for each input file. With the -v, --invert-match option, count non-matching lines.

options.name: --color
options.description: Surround the matched (non-empty) strings, matching lines, context lines, file names, line numbers, byte offsets, and separators (for fields and groups of contex…

name: -L
--files-without-match
options.description: Suppress normal output; instead print the name of each input file from which no output would normally have been printed.

name: -l
--files-with-matches
options.description: Suppress normal output; instead print the name of each input file from which output would normally have been printed.

name: -m
--max-count
options.description: Stop reading a file after NUM matching lines.

name: -o
--only-matching
options.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of a matching line, with each such part on a separate output line

name: -q
--quiet
--silent
options.description: Quiet; do not write anything to standard output. Exit immediately with zero status if any match is found, even if an error was detected.

name: -s
--no-messages
options.description: Suppress error messages about nonexistent or unreadable files.

name: -b
--byte-offset
options.description: Print the 0-based byte offset within the input file before each line of output.

name: -H
--with-filename
options.description: Print the file name for each match. This is the default when there is more than one file to search

name: -h
--no-filename
options.description: Suppress the prefixing of file names on output. This is the default when there is only one file (or only standard input) to search

options.name: --label
options.description: Display input actually coming from standard input as input coming from file LABEL.

name: -n
--line-number
options.description: Prefix each line of output with the 1-based line number within its input file. (-n is specified by POSIX.)

name: -T
--initial-tab
options.description: Make sure that the first character of actual line content lies on a tab stop, so that the alignment of tabs looks normal.

name: -u
--unix-byte-offsets
options.description: Report Unix-style byte offsets. This switch causes grep to report byte offsets as if the file were a Unix-style text file, i.e., with CR characters stripped off…

options.name: --null
options.description: Output a zero byte (the ASCII NUL character) instead of the character that normally follows a file name.

name: -A
--after-context
options.description: Print num lines of trailing context after each match

name: -B
--before-context
options.description: Print num lines of leading context before each match. See also the -A and -C options

name: -C
--context
options.description: Print NUM lines of output context. Places a line containing a group separator (--) between contiguous groups of matches.

name: -a
--text
options.description: Treat all files as ASCII text. Normally grep will simply print ``Binary file ... matches'' if files contain binary characters.

options.name: --binary-files
options.description: Controls searching and printing of binary files

suggestions.name: binary
suggestions.description: Search binary files but do not print them

name: -D
--devices
options.description: Specify the demanded action for devices, FIFOs and sockets

suggestions.name: read
suggestions.description: Read as if they were normal files

name: -d
--directories
options.description: Specify the demanded action for directories

suggestions.name: read
suggestions.description: Directories are read in the same manner as normal files

options.name: --exclude
options.description: Note that --exclude patterns take priority over --include patterns, and if no --include pattern is specified, all files are searched that are not excluded.

options.name: --exclude-dir
options.description: If -R is specified, only directories matching the given filename pattern are searched.

options.name: -I
options.description: Ignore binary files. This option is equivalent to --binary-file=without-match option

options.name: --include
options.description: If specified, only files matching the given filename pattern are searched. Note that --exclude patterns take priority over --include patterns.

options.name: --include-dir
options.description: If -R is specified, only directories matching the given filename pattern are searched.

name: -R
-r
--recursive
options.description: Recursively search subdirectories listed

options.name: --line-buffered
options.description: Force output to be line buffered. By default, output is line buffered when standard output is a terminal and block buffered otherwise

name: -U
--binary
options.description: Search binary files, but do not attempt to print them

name: -J
-bz2decompress
options.description: Decompress the bzip2(1) compressed file before looking for the text

name: -V
--version
options.description: Print version number of grep to the standard output stream

name: -P
--perl-regexp
options.description: Interpret pattern as a Perl regular expression

name: -f
--file
options.description: Obtain patterns from FILE, one per line. The empty file contains zero patterns, and therefore matches nothing. (-f is specified by POSIX.)

additionalSuggestions.name: -RIn
additionalSuggestions.description: Search for a pattern [R]ecursively in the current directory, showing matching line [n]umbers, [I]gnoring non-text files

additionalSuggestions.name: -Hn
additionalSuggestions.description: Print file name with the corresponding line number (n) for each match
